## Highlights

- Make full scans more predictable by bounding hidden-parameter discovery, parallelizing cross-endpoint transfer and raising the full crawler capacity to 1,500 pages.
- Expand SSRF coverage across major cloud metadata providers and internal service fingerprints while retaining provider-specific false-positive controls.
- Harden OAST correlation so every blind SSRF/WAF probe has its own one-time identity and callbacks issued before provider failover remain valid.
- Disable blind coverage when the end-to-end OAST health check fails instead of continuing with an unusable listener.
- Improve automatic memory sizing and make terminal resource telemetry easier to read.

## Verification and reliability

- Correct malformed PDF injection and Server-Side JavaScript callback URLs.
- Strengthen blind XSS, SQLi, command injection, LFI, DOM XSS, HTTP smuggling and source-disclosure verification.
- Preserve complete callback evidence without allowing a later probe to overwrite the payload responsible for an OAST interaction.
- Add regression coverage for OAST failover, health failure, per-payload identities, expanded SSRF providers and protocol-smuggling behavior.
- Keep the strict observed benchmark fail-closed and publish the complete-corpus coverage audit so missing module fixtures remain explicit while the corpus is expanded.

## Install with Go

The `engine/v0.2.6` module tag makes both commands install this release:

```bash
go install github.com/akha-security/akca/engine/cmd/akca@v0.2.6
go install github.com/akha-security/akca/engine/cmd/akca@latest
```

## Downloads

- `akca-windows-amd64.exe` — Windows x64
- `akca-linux-amd64` — Linux x64
- `akca-linux-arm64` — Linux ARM64
- `akca-darwin-amd64` — macOS Intel
- `akca-darwin-arm64` — macOS Apple Silicon
- `SHA256SUMS.txt` — SHA-256 verification manifest

Release binaries include GitHub build-provenance attestations and can be verified with `gh attestation verify <binary> -R akha-security/akca`.

Browser-backed checks require Chrome, Chromium, or Edge. Use AKCA only against systems you own or are explicitly authorized to test.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/akha-security/akca/compare/v0.2.5...v0.2.6
